auth.title: Sign in to the control plane
auth.subtitle: Manage models, keys, routing and usage.
auth.noMethod: No login method is enabled for this deployment.
auth.selfHosted: Self-hosted · sessions are local to this deployment.
auth.sessionExpired: Your session expired — sign in again.

errors.invalidCredentials: That email and password do not match an account here.
errors.passwordLoginDisabled: Password sign-in is turned off for this organization. Use single sign-on below.
errors.tooManyAttempts: Too many failed attempts. Try again later.
errors.tooManyAttempts_wait_one: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {{count}} second.
errors.tooManyAttempts_wait_other: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {{count}} seconds.
errors.unavailable: The control plane could not be reached. Check that it is running and try again.

common.copyFailed: Copy failed — the clipboard is unavailable on this page

unauthenticated.title: Sign in to see {{resource}}
unauthenticated.body: Your session is missing or has expired, so the control plane refused the request. This is not a problem with the data.

forbidden.title: You do not have access to {{resource}}
forbidden.body: You are signed in, but your role does not permit reading this. Retrying will not help — ask an administrator to widen your role.

openMode.title: {{resource}} needs an admin token
openMode.body: The control plane is running with no admin token, so it has no accounts and cannot serve per-user data to anyone. Signing in will not fix this: set ROLTER_ADMIN_TOKEN and restart it.

noStore.title: {{resource}} needs a database on the control plane
noStore.body: This control plane is running from a config file alone, so the endpoint behind this screen is not mounted at all. Retrying or signing in will not change that: start it with a database (ROLTER_DATABASE_URL) to manage {{resource}} here, or keep editing rolter.toml.

noAnalytics.title: Analytics are not configured on this control plane
noAnalytics.body: It answered, and the answer was that it keeps no analytics store, so it cannot serve {{resource}}: it runs without CLICKHOUSE_URL, or is older than the endpoint behind this screen. Retrying or signing in will not change that — configure ClickHouse and restart it.

unreachable.title: Cannot reach the control plane
unreachable.body: The request for {{resource}} got no answer at all. Check that the control plane is running and that this dashboard points at the right address.

server.title: The control plane failed to return {{resource}}
server.body: It answered, and the answer was an error. Its own message is below; the server logs will have more.

unknown.title: Could not load {{resource}}
unknown.body: The control plane rejected the request for a reason the dashboard does not recognise. Its own message is below.

modelSheet.currencyUnconvertible: {{code}} has no conversion rate configured, so this price cannot be converted to {{base}} and will not reach spend or budgets. Add it to [currency.rates] in the bootstrap config, or price in {{base}}.
modelSheet.pricingDocs: Rolter docs: how request cost is calculated ↗
modelSheet.advancedRejected: The control plane refused this model's advanced configuration: {{message}}. Everything else was saved.
modelSheet.subtitleAdd: Register a model and how the gateway calls it.
modelSheet.readonlyNotice: Read-only config model — defined in config and always present. Fields are shown for reference; edits and deletes are rejected with <0>409 Conflict</0>.

dupFrom.label: Duplicate from
dupFrom.info: Prefill every field from an existing model, then tweak. Handy for adding a second deployment of the same model on another provider.

sections.paramsInfo: Server-side default values for inference parameters, and whether clients may override each one.
sections.capsInfo: What this model endpoint supports. Flags gate request features and hint the playground — they don't add capabilities the provider lacks. The set shown depends on the model type.
sections.pricingInfo: Override the datasheet price for accurate cost tracking. All fields optional — blank counts as 0.
sections.headersInfo: Extra HTTP headers sent upstream with every request. Same lock rules as parameters — control whether clients can override them.

fields.providerInfo: The upstream provider that serves this model. Sets auth, endpoint shape, and which parameters are valid.
fields.modalityInfo: The modality this endpoint handles. Determines which request schema and playground surface apply.
fields.upstreamInfo: The exact model id the provider expects — this string is sent to the base URL. e.g. gpt-4o, claude-sonnet-4-20250514, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
fields.upstreamHint: Sent verbatim to the provider — must match their API exactly.
fields.upstreamHintEdit: Renaming isn't supported yet — delete and re-add to change the name.
fields.aliasInfo: Optional. The public name clients call this model by. Leave blank to reuse the upstream name. Use it to expose a stable, provider-agnostic name.
fields.aliasHint: The name clients send. Optional — defaults to the upstream name.
fields.baseUrlInfo: Point this model at a custom endpoint (self-hosted, proxy, or region). Leave blank to use the provider's default base URL.
fields.baseUrlHint: Optional. Overrides the provider endpoint for this model only.
fields.descriptionInfo: Free text shown in the catalog and pickers. Note capabilities, intended use, or gotchas for your team.
fields.descriptionPlaceholder: What is this model for? Any routing notes for the team…
fields.enabledHint: Off = kept in the catalog but excluded from routing and pickers.

lock.noteLockAll: Locked: clients cannot override any parameter — these server-side values are enforced.
lock.noteUnlockAll: Open: clients may override any parameter. Values here act as defaults only.
lock.noteManual: Manual: lock individual parameters below; unlocked ones stay client-overridable.

caps.reasoningInfo: Extended-thinking model (o-series, R1). Enables the reasoning_effort parameter.

pricing.hint: Optional cost overrides for accurate tracking — fields shown match the model type. Leave blank for free / provider-tracked.

net.rpmInfo: Max requests per minute to this model. Blank = no per-model cap (virtual-key limits still apply).
net.tpmInfo: Max tokens per minute across requests to this model. Blank = no per-model cap.
net.weightInfo: Relative share of traffic when this model is one of several targets for the same alias.
net.insecureTlsHint: Disables cert verification for this model's endpoint.
net.insecureTlsInfo: Skip TLS certificate verification. Only for self-signed or private-CA endpoints you trust — never for public providers.
net.allowAdditionalHint: Forward unknown fields instead of stripping them.
net.allowAdditionalInfo: Pass through request fields not in Rolter's schema straight to the provider — for provider-specific options Rolter doesn't model yet.

rbac.minRoleInfo: The lowest role allowed to call this model. Members below this role won't see it in pickers or be able to invoke it.
rbac.visibilityInfo: Public = available to anyone meeting the minimum role. Restricted = only the teams, virtual keys, and users you list below.

errors.provider: Required. Pick the upstream provider that actually serves this model.
errors.upstream: Required. Enter the model id exactly as the provider's API expects it — this is the string sent to the base URL (e.g. gpt-4o, claude-sonnet-4-20250514).
errors.alias: A model named “{{name}}” already exists. Give this one a distinct Rolter alias.
errors.baseUrl: Base URL must start with http:// or https://. Leave blank to use the provider's default endpoint.
errors.param: One or more custom parameters have a value but no name — name them or clear the value.
errors.header: One or more custom headers have a value but no name — name them or clear the value.

dashboard.notConfiguredBody: Traffic, spend, and latency appear here once requests flow through the gateway. Set clickhouse_url on the control plane to enable logging.
dashboard.noSpendRecorded: No spend recorded for this window. Requests were served, but none of them were priced — add pricing for the models in use to see cost here.

unpriced.title_one: {{count}} request in this window is unpriced.
unpriced.title_other: {{count}} requests in this window are unpriced.
unpriced.body_one: They ran against {{count}} model with no price set, so spend below is a floor, not a total. Set a price to include them.
unpriced.body_other: They ran against {{count}} models with no price set, so spend below is a floor, not a total. Set prices to include them.

unpriced.hint: This model has no price row, so its traffic is recorded as unpriced rather than free. Its spend is missing from totals and budgets until a price is set.

models.emptyBody: A model is the public name clients call. Add one and point it at a provider, or ship it in the config file.
models.noMatchBody: Nothing matched the search and origin filters you have on.

providers.scopeBlocked: Add/edit/delete is unavailable: {{error}}. Read-only view still works.
providers.noOrg: No org configured yet — pick or create one to manage providers.
providers.deleteHint: <0>{{name}}</0> will stop being usable as a route target. This cannot be undone.
providers.emptyBody: A provider is an upstream the gateway can route to. Add one with its API base and credential to start serving traffic.
providers.noMatchBody: Nothing matched your search. Clear it to see every provider in this organization.

plugins.heading: Installed plugins
plugins.intro: Request and response middleware the gateway consults on live traffic. Enabled plugins run at their stage, in position order.
plugins.noOrg: Choose an organization to manage plugins.
plugins.emptyDescription: Install a webhook plugin and choose its pipeline stage. It only affects traffic once you enable it.
plugins.stageEmpty: No plugin configured at this stage

pre_route.label: Pre-route
pre_route.description: Inspect or enrich the request before rolter selects a route.

pre_upstream.label: Pre-upstream
pre_upstream.description: Transform the routed request immediately before provider delivery.

post_response.label: Post-response
post_response.description: Inspect or transform the provider response before client delivery.

plugins.dialogDescription: Set the pipeline position and failure behavior. Secret values stay in gateway environment variables.
plugins.hintSecret: Store the variable name, never the secret value.
plugins.hintConfig: A JSON object sent to the plugin on every dispatch.
plugins.enabledHint: An enabled plugin is consulted on live traffic at its stage. Paused plugins keep their configuration but are skipped.
plugins.errorConfigObject: Configuration must be a JSON object.
plugins.errorNameEndpoint: Name and an HTTP(S) endpoint are required.

confirm.title: Delete {{name}}?
confirm.body: The gateway stops consulting this plugin immediately, at every stage it was configured for.

strategyHints.needsTelemetry: Needs a cache-telemetry source (KV events or an LMCache controller) configured on the target providers. Without one it quietly falls back to least-load.
strategyHints.deploymentWide: Controlled by the deployment-wide adaptive-routing policy, not from here. Kept so this route is not changed by saving.

confirm.title: Delete route {{model}}?
confirm.body: Clients calling this model name stop resolving to any provider the moment the route is gone.

routing.emptyBody: A route is the public model name clients call, resolved to one or more upstream targets by its strategy.

pricing.unconvertible: Priced in {{code}}, which has no conversion rate — this model's spend is missing from {{base}} totals and budgets.
pricing.emptyBody: Without a price a model's traffic is recorded as unpriced, so its spend is missing from totals and budgets.

playground.modelsNeedKey: Showing configured routes. Set a virtual key above to list what the gateway actually serves — provider-pinned and provider-group addresses only appear in the gateway's list.
playground.modelsUnreachable: Could not read the gateway's model list with this key, so configured routes are shown instead. Provider-pinned and provider-group addresses are missing from this list.
playground.pcaChartAria: PCA projection of the embedded texts
playground.embedEmpty: Embed some texts to see them projected to 2D.
playground.transcribeEmpty: Upload an audio file to transcribe.

promptRepo.renameDescription: The slug {{slug}} is the stable identity and never changes. Versions and scopes are untouched.
promptRepo.deleteLive: v{{version}} is live — anything routing through this template starts failing immediately.
promptRepo.deleteUnpublished: This template has never been published.
promptRepo.deleteConsequence: Every version, scope and sample is deleted with it. This cannot be undone.
promptRepo.created: Template created. Add its first immutable draft.
promptRepo.draftSaved: Draft v{{version}} saved. Its content and scopes are now immutable.
promptRepo.draftSavedScopeError: Draft v{{version}} was saved, but its scopes were not: {{error}}
promptRepo.rolledBack: Rolled back: v{{version}} is live again.
promptRepo.problemInvalidName: “{{name}}” is not a valid variable name.
promptRepo.problemRequiredDefault: Required variable “{{name}}” cannot also have a default.
promptRepo.emptyDescription: Create a named template, then add variables, ordered decorators, and its first deployment scope.
promptRepo.variablesDescription: Declare placeholders used as {{sample}} inside decorators.
promptRepo.noVariables: No variables. This template renders the same content for every request.
promptRepo.decoratorsDescription: Build ordered messages around the caller's original conversation.
promptRepo.scopesDescription: Choose where this exact version can be resolved. Empty means it is not assigned.
promptRepo.previewDescription: Sample values stay in your browser and are never saved.
promptRepo.missingSamples: Add sample values for {{names}} to complete the preview.
promptRepo.addDecoratorHint: Add a decorator to see the rendered prompt.
promptRepo.createDescription: The slug is a stable identity. Content is added as an immutable version next.
promptRepo.rollbackDescription: This changes the live version from v{{from}} to immutable v{{to}}. The newer versions remain in history.

skillsRepo.deletePublished: v{{version}} is published — agents resolving this skill start failing immediately.
skillsRepo.deleteUnpublished: This skill has never been published.
skillsRepo.deleteConsequence: Every version and access rule is deleted with it. Retire it instead if you only want it hidden.
skillsRepo.created: Skill created. Add its first immutable version.
skillsRepo.versionSaved: Version v{{version}} saved. Its content and metadata are now immutable.
skillsRepo.publishedNotice: v{{version}} is now the resolved version.
skillsRepo.retiredNotice: Skill retired. It no longer resolves for callers.
skillsRepo.metadataNotObject: Metadata must be a JSON object.
skillsRepo.refScheme: Use an https, git+https, oci, or s3 reference.
skillsRepo.emptyDescription: Create an org skill, define who can resolve it, then save inline content or a credential-free artifact reference.
skillsRepo.contentSourceDescription: Store a complete SKILL.md inline or point to an immutable artifact without credentials.
skillsRepo.contentRefHint: Pin a digest or commit where the scheme supports it. Embedded credentials are rejected.
skillsRepo.versionMetadataDescription: Optional non-secret JSON for runtime requirements, capabilities, or provenance.
skillsRepo.secretFieldsRejected: Fields containing secret, password, token, or API key names are rejected by the control plane.
skillsRepo.allowedTeamsHint: No selection shares the skill with every team in the organization.
skillsRepo.retireHint: Callers can no longer resolve it. Versions remain in history.
skillsRepo.createDescription: Define its identity and access policy. Content is saved as a separate immutable version.
skillsRepo.settingsDescription: Change the human-facing metadata and who can resolve this skill. The slug and versions stay immutable.
skillsRepo.rollbackDescription: This changes the resolved version from v{{from}} to immutable v{{to}}. Newer versions remain in history.

confirm.title: Delete tool group {{name}}?
confirm.body: The bundle is removed and any client relying on it loses access to the tools it governed.

tool-groups.lead: Bundle exact server/tool pairs into reusable policy manifests. Groups define intended access; project assignment and gateway enforcement remain separate policy work.
tool-groups.emptyBody: Create a governed bundle from registered server tools.
tool-groups.emptyNoServers: Register MCP servers and declare their tools before creating a group.

dialog.lead: Select exact tools. A group is a policy manifest, not a credential.

virtualKeys.explainer: Virtual keys are the credential clients send to the gateway (sk-rolter-…). Provider keys — the credentials your providers issued to rolter — live on the Providers screen and are never sent by clients.
virtualKeys.emptyBody: A virtual key is the credential your applications send to the gateway. Create one to start authenticating them.
virtualKeys.noMatchBody: Nothing matched your search. Clear it to see every key in this project.
virtualKeys.editSubtitleHint: Renaming and re-scoping a key are not offered: the control plane cannot change either after the secret is issued.

acceptInvite.invalidLink: This invitation link is not valid. It may have been used, revoked, or expired — ask whoever invited you for a new one.
acceptInvite.title: Join {{org}}
acceptInvite.intro: You were invited as {{email}} with the {{role}} role. Choose a password — only you will know it.
acceptInvite.mismatch: The two passwords do not match.

channels.emptyBody: Add a webhook destination — Slack, PagerDuty, email or a custom endpoint — so rules have somewhere to deliver.
channels.sheetSubtitle: Webhook endpoint alerts are POSTed to.

rules.emptyBody: Add a threshold or anomaly rule and Rolter evaluates it against gateway analytics every minute.
rules.emptyBodyNoChannel: Add a channel first, then a rule that delivers to it. Rules without a channel evaluate but never notify.
rules.sheetSubtitle: Fires when the signal crosses the threshold within the window.

history.emptyBody: Every notification a rule sends to a channel is recorded here, newest first.

confirm.channelBody: Alerts routed to this webhook stop being delivered, and every rule pointing at it loses its destination.
confirm.ruleBody: The gateway stops evaluating this rule, so the condition it watches goes unwatched.

collectorConfig.title: OpenTelemetry Collector config
collectorConfig.where: This is the document your collector runs. Rolter exports once, to that one collector; the config below is what fans what it receives out to every enabled connector, each pipeline with its own sampling and auth.
collectorConfig.emptyBody: With no connectors the config renders no exporters and no pipelines, so a collector running it would deliver nothing. Add a connector first.
collectorConfig.deploy: Save it as the collector's config file — infra/otel/collector.compose.yaml in the docker/docker-compose.observability.yml overlay — or point the collector straight at the URL above with --config and reload it on a schedule.

confirm.title: Delete connector {{name}}?
confirm.body: Request logs stop being shipped to this endpoint immediately, and its delivery history goes with it.

connectors.emptyBody: Add an OTLP/HTTP collector and request logs are mirrored to it — Datadog, Langfuse, or your own stack.

confirm.title: Delete profile {{name}}?
confirm.body: Every user and team assigned this profile loses the roles and model policy it carries, immediately.

accessProfiles.emptyBody: A profile bundles custom roles and a model policy, then hands the bundle to a user or a whole team.
accessProfiles.detailUnavailable: What this profile carries is unavailable
accessProfiles.sheetSubtitle: A profile bundles custom roles and a model policy. Assign it to a user or a team and everyone it reaches picks up both.
accessProfiles.slugHint: Derived from the name when left blank, and never renamed afterwards
accessProfiles.descriptionPlaceholder: Read-only access to logs and analytics
accessProfiles.rolesHint: Composed at organization scope, so the role applies across every team and project in it. A profile may only carry roles from its own org.
accessProfiles.rolesEmpty: This organization has no custom roles yet. Define one on Roles & Permissions first.
accessProfiles.policyHint: One pattern per line: an exact name, or a trailing-* prefix glob. Deny always beats allow.
accessProfiles.denyHint: Blocked even when a rule above allows it

oauth.title: OAuth client
oauth.lead: The client Rolter presents to this server's authorization server. Registering it is what makes Connect possible; nothing here mints a token.
oauth.secretHint: Write-only. Leave blank to keep the stored secret unchanged.
oauth.secretPlaceholder: Sealed — type a new value to rotate
oauth.clearingSecret: The stored secret is cleared on save, leaving a public client.
oauth.scopesHint: Requested when a consent flow does not name its own. Comma or newline separated.
oauth.redirectHint: Register this exact callback with the authorization server; it is derived from the deployment, never from the browser.
oauth.endpointError: Must be an https URL (http is accepted only on loopback).
oauth.incomplete: An OAuth client needs an authorization URL, a token URL and a client ID together.

connect.unconfigured: Register an OAuth client on this server before connecting.
connect.startedDetail: Finish the approval in the new tab. The session appears on Auth Sessions once it completes.
connect.blockedDetail: Allow pop-ups for this dashboard, then start the flow again.

mcpCatalog.noOrgBody: MCP servers are isolated by organization.
mcpCatalog.registryHint: Registered servers are projected into the gateway snapshot when enabled.
mcpCatalog.emptyBody: Register a custom endpoint or install a curated server from MCP Library.

confirmDelete.title: Delete {{name}}?
confirmDelete.body: Deleting this server also removes every OAuth grant and token session attached to it. This cannot be undone.

dialog.lead: Declare the endpoint and exact tool names exposed through the organization registry.

confirm.sessionBody: The token behind this session stops working at once. The consent it was minted under stands, so a new session can be created without asking the user again.
confirm.grantBody: Revoking this grant for <0>{{server}}</0> also revokes {{sessions}} under it, in the same transaction. The user must consent again before the server can be called on their behalf.

mcpOAuth.noOrgBody: {{resource}} are scoped to one organization. Pick or create one to view them.
mcpOAuth.grantsEmptyBody: A grant appears the first time a user completes the OAuth flow for an MCP server. Nothing is created here — consent is only ever given by the user.
mcpOAuth.sessionsEmptyBody: A session is minted when a user's consent is exchanged for a token. Start one with Connect on MCP Catalog — the session appears here as soon as the user approves.

grants.revokeTitle: Revoke this consent and every session under it

sessions.revokeTitle: Revoke this session; the consent behind it stands

mcpOAuth.grantsTokenNotice: A grant records consent, not credentials. No access or refresh token is ever sent to this dashboard — the sealed tokens stay inside the control plane, and revoking consent here is what makes them unusable.
mcpOAuth.sessionsTokenNotice: Sessions are shown as metadata only. The access and refresh tokens are sealed with the deployment key and never leave the control plane, so this screen can tell you a session is renewable but never what it holds.
mcpOAuth.sessionsFootnote: Revoking a session leaves the consent in place — a new session can be minted without asking the user again. To withdraw consent itself, revoke the grant on OAuth Grants.
mcpOAuth.scopeNoteGrants: Org admins see every grant in the org; members and viewers see — and may revoke — only their own.
mcpOAuth.scopeNoteSessions: Org admins see every session in the org; members and viewers see — and may revoke — only their own.

confirm.title: Forget node {{id}}?
confirm.body: The node is dropped from the inventory. If it is still running it reappears on its next snapshot poll.

cluster.emptyBody: Nodes appear here once a gateway identifies itself on its snapshot poll. A gateway sends its identity only when ROLTER_NODE_ID or HOSTNAME is set in its environment — containers always have HOSTNAME; a bare-metal or native run needs ROLTER_NODE_ID set explicitly.

confirm.title: Delete {{name}}?
confirm.unitBody: The business unit is removed outright and the spend already attributed to it loses its label. Retire it instead to keep the history.
confirm.customerBody: The customer is removed outright and the spend already attributed to it loses its label. Retire it instead to keep the history.

costAttribution.unitEmptyBody: Business units roll teams up so spend can be attributed to the part of the organisation that incurred it.
costAttribution.customerEmptyBody: Customers attribute usage and spend to the people you serve, so it can be billed on or reported per account.

confirm.title: Delete {{name}}?
confirm.body: Gateway policy changes immediately: this rule stops being enforced on live traffic.

guardrailRules.heading: Traffic inspection rules
guardrailRules.intro: Rules run from the lowest position upward. Paused rules stay visible but never inspect traffic.
guardrailRules.emptyBody: Add a built-in detector or a bounded custom regex before enabling the deployment guardrails flag.
guardrailRules.dialogBody: Use a built-in detector or one bounded regular expression. The gateway validates it before publishing.
guardrailRules.patternHint: Uses the gateway’s linear-time regex engine.
guardrailRules.toggleEnabledHint: Paused rules remain stored and ordered.
guardrailRules.toggleSystemHint: Off by default because operator-authored instructions are trusted.

confirm.title: Delete {{name}}?
confirm.body: External enforcement through this provider stops immediately; traffic it was screening is no longer sent to it.

guardrailProviders.heading: Guardrail provider registry
guardrailProviders.intro: Register services freely; activate one at a time. Enabling a provider atomically hands enforcement over from the current service.
guardrailProviders.activeFailClosed: Requests stop when the service cannot decide.
guardrailProviders.activeFailOpen: Requests continue when the service cannot decide.
guardrailProviders.emptyBody: Register a self-hosted HTTP guardrail service. Credentials remain environment references, never stored secret values.
guardrailProviders.dialogBody: Use an HTTP endpoint and reference credentials by environment variable. Activating this provider pauses the current one.
guardrailProviders.urlHint: The gateway posts a vendor-neutral decision envelope.
guardrailProviders.envHint: Only the variable name is stored.
guardrailProviders.activateHint: Takes enforcement ownership from the currently active provider.
guardrailProviders.failOpenWarning: Fail-open favors availability: traffic continues if this provider times out or errors.

adaptiveDashboard.emptyBody: A gateway appears here after it serves a route on the adaptive strategy and reports to the control plane. Reports older than {{seconds}} seconds are hidden.

rbac.intro: Every guarded route names one resource:action pair, and the control plane serves this table from the same list it enforces with — so a cell here is the rule, not a description of it.
rbac.unknownGrants_one: {{count}} grant on a custom role names a resource this build does not define. It allows nothing.
rbac.unknownGrants_other: {{count}} grants on custom roles name resources this build does not define. They allow nothing.

baseRoles.admin: Admin — full control of the scope

custom.intro: An org-defined role is one of the built-in three plus the exact resource:action pairs it should also allow. A grant only ever widens: nothing the base role already permits can be taken away by one.
custom.emptyBody: Define a role once, compose it into an access profile, and hand that profile to a user or a whole team.
custom.noGrants: No explicit grants — the base role alone
custom.sheetSubtitle: Pick the built-in role it extends, then tick the exact pairs it should also allow.
custom.slugHint: Derived from the name when left blank, and never renamed afterwards
custom.descriptionPlaceholder: Read everything, mint keys for one customer
custom.baseRoleHint: The floor this role starts from. Every grant below is on top of it.
custom.grantsHint: One row per resource the deployment guards, straight from the capability table the control plane enforces with.
custom.superadminHint: Deployment-wide actions are superadmin-only and no custom role can grant them.
custom.unknownCarried_one: {{count}} grant names a resource this build does not define. It allows nothing, and saving keeps it as it is.
custom.unknownCarried_other: {{count}} grants name resources this build does not define. They allow nothing, and saving keeps them as they are.

confirm.title: Delete custom role {{name}}?
confirm.body: Everyone holding it through an access profile loses the pairs it grants. The base role they already had is untouched.
confirm.referenced: It is still composed into {{profiles}}. Detach it there first — the control plane refuses the delete until you do.

policy.title: Org sign-in policy
policy.subtitle: Which ways into the dashboard this organization allows. The superadmin can always sign in with a password, so an identity-provider outage cannot lock the deployment out.
policy.passwordHint: Members sign in with an email and a password. Turning this off needs an enabled identity provider first — the control plane refuses it otherwise.
policy.ssoHint: Members sign in through a registered identity provider. The sign-in screen shows one button per enabled provider.
policy.bothOff: At least one sign-in method has to stay on — both off is an outage, not a policy.

providers.title: Identity providers
providers.defaultRole: Signs in as {{role}} when no group mapping matches.
providers.noDefaultRole: No default role: a user in no mapped group is refused, rather than admitted with nothing.
providers.noSecretHint: No client secret is sealed for this provider, so the token exchange will fail at login. Re-register it with a secret, or check that ROLTER_KEK was set when it was created.
providers.clearSecretNamed: Remove the stored client secret for {{name}}
providers.secretClearedToast: {{name}} no longer has a stored client secret

empty.title: No identity provider yet
empty.body: Register your OIDC provider and members sign in with the company account they already have — rolter turns the groups in their id token into roles here, so joiners and leavers are handled in the directory instead of one invitation at a time.

confirm.title: Delete provider {{name}}?
confirm.body: Anyone signing in through it loses that route immediately, and its group mappings go with it. Accounts it already created stay, with the roles they already hold.

clearSecret.title: Remove the stored client secret for {{name}}?
clearSecret.body: The provider becomes a public client relying on PKCE alone from the next sign-in. If your identity provider still expects a secret, every login through it fails until you enter a new one — and the removed secret cannot be read back, here or anywhere else.

create.title: Add identity provider
create.subtitle: OIDC · authorization code with PKCE
create.name: Name
create.nameHint: What the button on the sign-in screen says.
create.slugHint: Appears in the login URL, so keep it short — it cannot be changed later.
create.issuerHint: The provider's OIDC issuer. Its discovery document and signing keys are read from here.
create.clientIdHint: The application your provider registered for rolter.
create.clientSecretHint: Leave empty for a public client that relies on PKCE alone.
create.secretWriteOnly: The secret is sealed the moment it is saved and is never shown again — not on this screen, not through the API. To change it, edit the provider and enter a new one.
create.scopesHint: Space-separated. Leave empty for openid email profile.
create.groupClaimHint: The claim in the id token carrying the user's groups. Leave empty for groups.
create.defaultRoleHint: Granted when no group mapping matches. Leave unset to refuse those users instead.

edit.title: Edit identity provider
edit.subtitle: Rotate the client secret, correct the issuer, or take the provider out of service. Group mappings and the provider's id are kept.
edit.slugImmutable: The slug is in the login URL, so it cannot be changed. A provider that needs a different one is a different provider.
edit.clientSecretHint: Leave empty to keep the stored secret — whitespace alone counts as empty and changes nothing. Enter a new one to rotate it. The stored secret is never shown, here or anywhere else; to drop it entirely, use Remove stored secret on the provider's card.

mcpSettings.lead: Defaults apply when registering new MCP servers. Runtime authorization still comes from server scopes and each user’s OAuth session.
mcpSettings.failureModeHint: Stored as the intended policy for clients that consume MCP settings.
mcpSettings.allowUnlistedHint: Permit clients to request tools not declared in the registry manifest.
mcpSettings.persistNote: These values are persisted for MCP-aware clients. The current HTTP proxy continues to use deployment-level transport timeouts.

logsSettings.captureOffSummary: Nothing is stored: no prompt or completion text is retained for any request. Log metadata — model, tokens, cost, latency, status — is unaffected and keeps flowing.
logsSettings.captureOnSummary: Stored: the raw prompt and completion body of each matching request, truncated at {{bytes}} bytes, kept for {{hours}} hours and then deleted. Redacted before writing: {{redacted}}. Models captured: {{models}}.
logsSettings.sampleRateHint: Percentage of requests written to the log. Lower it to cut storage on high-volume deployments; metrics and budgets are unaffected.
logsSettings.captureHint: Store raw prompt and completion bodies alongside the log metadata. Off by default — payloads carry whatever the caller sent.
logsSettings.maxBytesHint: Anything longer is truncated. Maximum 1048576 (1 MiB).
logsSettings.redactedHint: Comma-separated JSON keys stripped from captured payloads before they are stored. Redaction happens before the write, so a redacted value never reaches storage.
logsSettings.onlyModelsHint: Comma-separated model names. Leave empty to capture payloads for every model.
logsSettings.onlyKeysHint: Comma-separated virtual key UUIDs. Leave empty to capture payloads for every key.
logsSettings.retentionHint: How long each half of the log is kept. Payloads are the sensitive half, so they cannot outlive the metadata they belong to.

errors.sampleRange: Sample rate must be between 0 and 100 percent.
errors.maxBytes: Max payload bytes must be a whole number between 0 and 1048576.
errors.retentionDays: Retention must be a whole number of days between 1 and 3650.
errors.payloadRetentionHours: Payload retention must be a whole number of hours between 1 and 8760.
errors.payloadOutlivesLog: Payload retention cannot outlive log retention.

clientSettings.baseUrlHint: The address clients point their SDK at. Set this when the gateway sits behind a load balancer or a custom domain, so the snippet below matches what a caller can actually reach. Leave it empty to use this dashboard’s own origin.
clientSettings.forwardedHint: Inbound client headers passed through to the upstream provider, comma or newline separated. Everything not listed is dropped at the gateway.
clientSettings.injectedHint: Static headers the gateway adds to every upstream request. A trace-context header of the same name still wins, so correlation cannot be broken from here. Values are treated as deployment secrets and are never written to the audit log.
clientSettings.injectedNone: No headers injected — upstream requests carry only what the gateway and the caller already send.
clientSettings.correlationHint: Header carrying the end-to-end request id. The gateway reuses the caller’s value when present, mints one when absent, and echoes it on the response so a client can find its own call in the logs.

errors.baseUrlScheme: Base URL must start with http:// or https://.
errors.badHeaderName: '{{name}}' is not a valid header name.
errors.controlCharacters: Value for '{{name}}' must not contain control characters.
errors.tooManyForwarded: At most 64 forwarded headers are allowed.
errors.tooManyInjected: At most 64 injected headers are allowed.
errors.badRequestIdHeader: Request ID header is not a valid header name.

security.dashboardAuthHint: Require a credential to open the dashboard. Provide either an external secret-manager reference or a managed secret stored encrypted.
security.secretHint: Write-only: the secret is encrypted server-side and never shown again.
security.enforceVkHint: Require a virtual key for all inference requests.
security.allowedOriginsHint: Comma-separated list of exact http(s) origins allowed for CORS and WebSocket connections. Wildcards are rejected — list each origin explicitly.
security.allowedHeadersHint: Comma-separated list of allowed headers for CORS.
security.requiredHeadersHint: Comma-separated name: value pairs that must be present on every request. Requests missing any of them are rejected.
security.bypassRoutesHint: Comma-separated exact /v1 paths that skip the auth middleware. System routes like /health and the login endpoints are always open.
